title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the 1986 axiomatic 'Analysis situs' notes. The basic structure is a 'magasin' (also called 'inégalité' on the next page): a set M of 'pieces' (think closed cells or closed polyhedra) equipped with several relations.
- ≤ is an order, roughly inclusion.
- X ∘< Y is a 'strict interior' relation.
- X |∘| Y and X |·| Y are 'disjointness' relations. In context, X |·| Y reads as 'X and Y have disjoint (relative) interiors'.
- ≪ and ∥ are further relations.

Figures. X̃ = M_{≤X} denotes the down-set (closure) of X. A figure F is a closed (down-closed) subset F̃ of M whose distinct members are pairwise |·|. It is the analogue of a regular cell complex: a finite family of cells, closed under taking faces, whose open cells are disjoint.

A figure indexed by a poset I is an order isomorphism I ≅ F̃, written i ↦ X_i.

The page reformulates this as a map φ : I → M. Such a φ is increasing for ≤ and determines F through F̃ = φ(I).

Grothendieck asks which φ arise this way. Directly, one needs:
- (a) φ is injective and induces an order isomorphism I ≅ φ(I);
- (b) φ(I) is a figure, meaning (1°) a pairwise-disjointness condition on the X_i (transcribed 'X_i ≱ X_j') and (2°) φ(I) is closed in M.

Proposition. φ : I → M defines a figure indexed by I iff:
- (a) φ is increasing and injective;
- (b) for every i, the induced map I_{≤i} → X̃_i = M_{≤X_i} is an isomorphism of ordered sets;
- (c) i ≠ j ⇒ X_i |·| X_j.

Grothendieck notes that the hypothesis in (c), i ≠ j, is exactly i |·| j for the trivial magasin structure on I, defined on the previous page: any poset becomes a magasin with |∘| meaning ≠.

Proof (finished on the next page). Condition (b) gives φ(I) = ∪ M_{≤X_i}, so φ(I) is closed. Disjointness of distinct elements X', Y' of φ(I) comes from writing them as X_{i'}, X_{j'} with i' ≠ j' and applying (c). Order reflection also follows: X_i ≤ X_j puts X_i in M_{≤X_j} = φ(I_{≤j}), and injectivity then gives i ≤ j.

In categorical language, condition (b) says φ is a discrete fibration of posets that is also surjective on lower sets of images. Together with injectivity, this makes φ an isomorphism of I onto a sieve of M.

Purpose. This prepares the definition of morphisms of magasins (next page). It recasts figures as structure-respecting maps from a trivial magasin, i.e. as 'local isomorphisms' (étale-like maps) from a combinatorial index poset. This is the kind of combinatorial 'tame topology' foundation announced in the Esquisse.
errors: Condition 1°) is transcribed as 'X_i ≱ X_j'. Read literally for all i, j, it cannot hold (take i = j, or i < j). The intended condition, as the proof on the next page and condition (c) show, is pairwise disjointness of interiors |·| for distinct elements. This is either a slip of the pen or a misreading.
Minor redundancy: if |·| is irreflexive on nonempty pieces, condition (c) already forces injectivity in (a). This is harmless.
In the struck-out draft the conditions are labelled a), b) twice, then b), c). The final Proposition is consistent and correct as stated.

ideas.what: Figures in a magasin as down-closed families of pieces with pairwise disjoint interiors, indexed by a poset (face poset)
ideas.modern_name: Regular CW complex / face poset; CW posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Björner (CW posets, 1984); classical regular cell complexes (Whitehead, Cooke–Finney)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of 'tame topology' / dévissage of stratified structures in Esquisse d'un programme (1984). The magasin axiomatics is unpublished.

ideas.what: Characterisation of indexed figures as injective increasing maps φ: I→M inducing isomorphisms on lower sets, with distinct indices mapped to interior-disjoint pieces
ideas.modern_name: Sieve inclusion / discrete fibration of posets; local isomorphism of posets

ideas.what: Viewing the indexing poset I as a 'trivial magasin' (≠ as disjointness), so that a figure becomes a kind of morphism from a trivial magasin to M
ideas.modern_name: Free/discrete structure on a poset; figures as morphisms (functor-of-points style)

missed.claim: The page is a small step in Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic 'magasin' framework for analysis situs, where cell complexes are morphisms from trivial magasins. The individual result is routine. The framework as a whole (the relations ≤, ∘<, |·|, ≪ on a set of pieces, with figures defined as local isomorphisms) is not documented in the literature.
missed.quote: c) Si i ≠ j (i.e. i |·| j pour la structure triviale sur I!) on a X_i |·| X_j
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for reconstructing Grothendieck's tame-topology programme. It is comparable to later combinatorial and o-minimal cell-complex axiomatics, but this page adds no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The proposition is a correct, elementary reformulation of what a face-poset-indexed cell complex is. It is only interesting as part of the unpublished magasin axiomatics.
transcription_corrections: '1°) ∀ i,j ∈ I, X_i ≱ X_j' is very likely 'X_i |·| X_j' (or a pairwise disjointness symbol) given the proof on the next page; the symbol in the image is ambiguous.
'pour la structure ordinaire[?] triviale sur I' — the image reads 'pour la structure de magasin triviale sur I!', referring to the trivial magasins of the previous page.
'En d'autres termes, [?] des X → X_i' — probably 'En d'autres termes, φ des X ↦ X_i' (the map i ↦ X_i), cut off.
